title: Theo and the Safehouse
premise: Petra Winterbourne, a crash investigator haunted by the death of her family in row twelve, receives a burner phone that plays recordings of her dead husband's voice — messages he left before the crash, revealing that Flight 447 was downed to silence a witness. The 'safehouse' is a network of ordinary people hiding that witness: a defector who can prove three governments conspired with a private arms consortium. Hunted by an assassin named Corvus who is himself a manufactured identity with no real past, Petra must smuggle the defector and the evidence to a tribunal in The Hague. In the end Petra exposes the conspiracy, discovers her husband was the conspiracy's first victim-turned-whistleblower, and chooses to build a new family with the safehouse's survivors rather than retreat into grief.
about_author: Bram Delacroix is the pen name of a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading crash reports and the silences between them. They write thrillers about paperwork, grief, and the violence hidden inside institutional language.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Two years after the crash, Petra works nights reconstructing wreckage, unable to sleep in her family's empty house. A routine inspection of Flight 447's tail section turns up a scorched burner phone that was never on the passenger manifest. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into professional suspicion.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The recovered phone rings at 3 a.m. On the line: her husband Daniel's voice, calm, pre-recorded, telling her that if she's hearing this, he didn't die in an accident. The message includes a coordinate in Rotterdam and the word 'safehouse.' Emotional beat: vertigo — hope and horror arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She pulls the full passenger list and finds eleven names that match no birth records — including seat 12C, directly beside her family. Her supervisor, Voss, gently suggests she take leave; his kindness feels rehearsed. Emotional beat: the first cold realization that someone is watching how she grieves.

chapters.title: Rotterdam, Low Tide
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra follows the coordinates to a shuttered canal house and meets Mara Ilic, a Bosnian forger, and Tomas, a teenage runaway who runs their radios. They are the safehouse — keepers of the witness, a man called only 'the Accountant.' Emotional beat: wary hospitality; Petra is a stranger being tested.

chapters.title: The Accountant
chapters.summary: Accountant's POV (first time). Hidden in the attic, the Accountant — a former consortium auditor named Elias Vane — reviews ledgers proving three governments laundered payments through the arms consortium that downed Flight 447 to silence him. Emotional beat: guilt; he has hidden while others died in row twelve.

chapters.title: Corvus
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. The assassin receives his contract: the Accountant, the safehouse, and now a crash investigator who asks too many questions. We learn he has no memories before his training — his identity was built, not born. Emotional beat: hollow professionalism masking a flicker of curiosity about Petra.

chapters.title: What Daniel Left
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Mara decrypts Daniel's phone: he was the consortium's logistics man who tried to blow the whistle, and the crash was meant to kill the Accountant — Daniel's death was collateral. Petra rages at the safehouse for knowing. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Voss Calls Again
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Her supervisor Voss invites her to a 'welfare meeting' that is clearly an interrogation; a consortium fixer sits behind him. Petra lies smoothly for the first time in her life and understands she has crossed a line. Emotional beat: terror and strange exhilaration.

chapters.title: Eleven Empty Seats
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The boy hacker traces the eleven ghost passengers: they were all prior whistleblowers, disappeared over a decade. One, he discovers, is still alive in a Prague care facility — a loose end Corvus is already en route to tie off. Emotional beat: Tomas finding purpose, and dread.

chapters.title: Prague, Room 41
chapters.summary: Petra and Tomas's POV. They reach the survivor, Halina, moments before Corvus does; a brutal, quiet escape through a hospital laundry leaves Halina's nurse dead and Petra holding the woman's hand as she dies. Emotional beat: the cost made flesh — Petra refuses to let more people die for her truth.

chapters.title: Halina's Testimony
chapters.summary: Halina's POV (single chapter). From a safehouse bed, Halina recounts the night in 2009 she signed off on the 'logistics exercise' that became Flight 447, and how the consortium rebuilt her as a warning. Her testimony completes the evidentiary chain. Emotional beat: an old woman choosing, at last, to be a witness.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Window
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Mara reveals the plan: the International Criminal Court's evidence window closes in nine days; after that, the consortium's pending 'restructuring' erases everything. The Accountant must testify in person. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline — the clock starts.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara drills the group: routes, dead drops, cover stories. Petra and the Accountant clash — he wants to surrender himself to end the danger; she refuses to let his guilt decide everyone's lives. Tomas quietly becomes the family's glue. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: Corvus Closes
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Corvus burns a consortium contact to find the Rotterdam house, feeling the first crack in his loyalty — his handlers lied about the Prague nurse. He watches the safehouse for two days and does not report the child. Emotional beat: the assassin's manufactured identity beginning to fail him.

chapters.title: The Canal House Falls
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Consortium operators raid the safehouse; Mara's contingencies save them, but the house burns and Mara is captured covering the retreat. Petra leads the survivors into the night with the evidence drive and Halina in a wheelchair. Emotional beat: loss, and the family holding together anyway.

chapters.title: Bargaining with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Petra and Corvus's POV, alternating. Petra contacts Corvus through an old handler channel and offers him what he's never had: his real file, his real name, in exchange for Mara's location. Emotional beat: two people with no past negotiating over the only currency that matters — identity.

chapters.title: The Handover
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. The exchange in an Antwerp freight yard goes wrong — Corvus's own handlers ambush it, revealing he was always meant to die with the witnesses. He kills his handlers, frees Mara, and vanishes with a copy of his own file. Emotional beat: an assassin choosing to become a person.

chapters.title: Nine Governments, Three Lies
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra and the Accountant make the run to The Hague through checkpoints, bribed border police, and a consortium-owned ferry, while Voss — revealed as the consortium's inside man in her own agency — hunts them personally. Emotional beat: the gauntlet; Petra stops running and starts hunting.

chapters.title: Voss at the Door
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Voss corners them at the tribunal's security perimeter, offering Petra a deal: her family's 'closure file' in exchange for the drive. She records his confession instead and lets him walk into the building where it will destroy him. Emotional beat: cold triumph; power turned back on its abusers.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Accountant's POV. Elias Vane testifies: ledgers, Halina's deposition, Daniel's recordings, Voss's confession. The chamber erupts as three governments' ministers are named. Corvus, unseen in the gallery, places his real name — a boy from Sarajevo — into the public record. Emotional beat: catharsis; truth spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Weeks later, Petra visits the crash site's memorial wall and finally sleeps a full night. She learns the full truth of Daniel's last message: 'Take care of them, and let them take care of you.' Emotional beat: grief transmuted into gratitude; the haunting ends.

chapters.title: The New Safehouse
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with the ensemble. Petra, Mara, Tomas, Halina, Elias, and Corvus share a too-small kitchen in Rotterdam, arguing about dinner — the safehouse reborn as a home rather than a hiding place. Petra pins Daniel's burner phone to the wall, its work done. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; family chosen, not lost.
